name: 10s Tap Test
what: CNS readiness test measuring rapid unweighted foot contacts.
why: Assesses central nervous system fatigue and fast-twitch readiness.
cue: Tap your feet as fast as possible for 10 seconds. We want to see how fiery your nervous system is today.

name: Broad Jump Drop-off
why: Identifies neuromuscular fatigue and force production capacity.
cue: Give me one max effort jump. If you're down more than a few inches, we're pulling back the heavy weights.

name: Subjective Wellness
why: Captures psycho-social stress and perceived recovery.
cue: Be honest on the questionnaire. Your sleep and stress levels dictate how hard we can push you today.

name: French Contrast Method
what: 4-exercise sequence combining heavy compound, plyometric, speed, and assisted plyo.
why: Maximizes rate of force development through post-activation potentiation.
cue: We're tricking your muscles into firing harder. Heavy lift first, then we fly.

name: Short-SSC (Ankle Stiffness)
why: Improves Achilles tendon elasticity and reactive strength.
cue: Stiff ankles like springs. Don't let your heels touch the ground.

name: Helical Slings (Cross-body)
what: Rotational movements connecting opposite hip and shoulder.
why: Trains the fascial slings responsible for throwing and striking power.
cue: Whip your hip and shoulder together. Power transfers across your body.

name: MAS (Maximal Aerobic Speed) 15s/15s
why: Increases aerobic capacity and VO2 max efficiently.
cue: 15 seconds on, 15 seconds off. Hit the distance marker every time.

name: Deadmill Sprints
why: High-resistance sprint training for acceleration mechanics.
cue: Drive the belt backward. Big arms, aggressive knees.

name: Lactic "Shandy"
why: Builds tolerance to blood lactate accumulation.
cue: It's going to burn. Embrace the lactic acid and keep moving.

name: Max Effort Method (Week 1)
cue: We're teaching your brain to fire every single muscle fiber at the exact same time so you generate pure power without getting bulky.

name: Repeat Effort Method (Week 2)
what: Lifting moderate loads (60-80% 1RM) for 8-12 reps to near failure.
why: Triggers structural hypertrophy, increases tendon cross-sectional area, local muscular endurance.
cue: This is armor-building week. We're thickening your tendons and muscles so they don't tear when you lunge for a ball in the 3rd set.

name: Dynamic Effort Method (Week 3)
what: Lifting sub-maximal loads (30-50% 1RM) or bodyweight at maximum possible velocity.
why: Increases the Rate of Force Development (RFD).
cue: Today isn't about how much weight you can move; it's about how fast you can move it.
